holds.name: dtolnay/rust-toolchain
holds.reason: Held on 2026-11-11: the action's only release tag is v1; a dated nightly toolchain input (rust-toolchain.toml pins a nightly-YYYY-MM-DD date) must be passed as the toolchain input with dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master, because the action otherwise derives the toolchain from the @rev (stable, beta, nightly, 1.x.y), so the sweep's 'beta -> v1' suggestion does not apply.
holds.evidence: https://github.com/dtolnay/rust-toolchain README (master, read 2026-11-11): 'When passing an explicit toolchain as an input instead of @rev, you'll want to use "dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master" as the revision of the action.'; GitHub tags API for dtolnay/rust-toolchain lists v1 only (2026-11-11).

holds.name: python
holds.reason: Held on 2026-11-11: the pyHanko job installs its hash-pinned closure (.github/conformance/pyhanko-requirements.txt) with --only-binary :all:, and the newest Python lines lack wheels in that closure: PyYAML 6.0.3 (its newest release) has no cp315 or cp316 wheel, lxml 6.1.3 and cffi 2.1.1 have no cp316 wheel; a source build of lxml needs libxml2 headers that the runner is not given. Move to 3.15 when PyYAML publishes a cp315 manylinux x86_64 wheel (then regenerate the requirements file with uv --python-version 3.15), and to 3.16 when lxml, cffi and PyYAML publish cp316 wheels.
holds.evidence: PyPI JSON API on 2026-11-11: PyYAML 6.0.3 manylinux x86_64 wheels cp314 1, cp315 0, cp316 0; lxml 6.1.3 cp314 2, cp315 1, cp316 0; cffi 2.1.1 cp314 1, cp315 1, cp316 0. actions/python-versions releases on 2026-11-11: 3.16.0-alpha.2 (newest on any channel), 3.15.2 (newest GA), 3.14.10 (newest 3.14).
